The Sub-Divisional Officer vs Tapan Bera @ Tapan Kumar Bera
& Ors on 15 April, 2024
Author: Arijit Banerjee

Bench: Arijit Banerjee
15.04.2024
Item No. 21.

Court No.6.
 Ab
 Mat 626 of 2023

With
 Can 1 of 2023
 Can 2 of 2023

The Sub-divisional Officer, Gosaba & Ors.
 Vs
 Tapan Bera @ Tapan Kumar Bera & Ors.
 Mr. Sirsanya Bandopadhyay,
 Ms. Tapati Samanta ....for the Appellants.

Dr. Debabrata Karan,
 Mr. Debopriyo Karan  Mr. Sankhasuvra Roy  Mr. Souvik Naiya .....for the Respondent/
Writ Petitioner.
In re : CAN 1 of 2023 This is an application for condonation of delay of 189 days in filing the appeal.

Causes shown being sufficient, the delay is condoned.
CAN 1 of 2023 is, accordingly, disposed of.

In re : MAT 626 of 2023, IA CAN 2 of 2023 A judgment and order dated September 28, 2022, whereby the writ petition of the respondent no.1 herein, being WPA 7415 of 2022, was disposed of by a learned Single Judge of this Court, is under challenge in this appeal, at the instance of the Sub Divisional Officer, Gosaba and other Officers of the State of West Bengal.
It is not in dispute that land of the respondent no.1/writ petitioner has been utilized by the State Government for construction of a "ring bandh".

However, such land was not acquired by the State,
following due process of law.
Consequently, no compensation was paid to the writ petitioner.
Claiming compensation, the writ petitioner approached the learned Single Judge.

The learned Judge disposed of the writ petition with the following directions:

sentences.text:
"In view of the above, the writ petition is disposed of directing the 6th respondent to act in terms of the letter issued to him on 10.02.2015 by the Sub Divisional Officer,
Gosaba Irrigation Sub Division and initiate land acquisition proceedings under the Act of 2013 within two months from the date of communication of this order.

The 6th respondent is further directed to take the proceedings to its logical conclusion in accordance with law upon affording reasonable opportunity to all the interested parties including the petitioner and take necessary steps for payment of compensation to the petitioner at the earliest preferably within a period of six months thereafter."
Being aggrieved, the State has come up by way of this appeal.
Mr. Bandopadhyay, learned Junior Standing Counsel says that the learned Judge should have granted the State the option of acquiring the land in question in terms of the State's Direct Purchase Policy.

If steps for acquisition are taken in terms of such policy, the writ petitioner will receive compensation at the market rate of the value of the property in question much sooner than if the State has to compute compensation in terms of the 2013 Act.
He seeks leave to produce a comparative calculation of compensation that the writ petitioner may receive following the two methods i.e. provisions of the 2013 Act and Direct Purchase Policy.
Learned Advocate for the respondent no.1/writ petitioner says that there is no error in the order of the learned Single Judge.
The law that presently governs acquisition of land by the State Government is the 2013 Act.
Hence, acquisition proceedings should be initiated and concluded expeditiously in accordance with the provisions of the 2013 Act.
Prima facie, we also do not find any infirmity in the order of the learned Single Judge.
However, on the request of Mr. Bandopadhyay, learned Junior Standing Counsel, we adjourn this matter for a week and direct it to be listed again on 23.4.2024.

(Arijit Banerjee, J.) (M. V. Muralidaran, J.)
